subject.title: [Feature]: Support for sandbox Docker parameters (--gpus all, --ipc=host)

question: Should OpenClaw expose host IPC for Docker sandboxes, and if yes should it be a narrow explicit `sandbox.docker.ipc` break-glass field instead of raw Docker argument passthrough?
rationale: Current source and release evidence show GPU passthrough is already implemented, while the remaining host IPC/raw-args request changes the sandbox isolation boundary and public config contract.

options.title: Approve a typed IPC break-glass field
options.body: Add a narrow opt-in IPC setting with schema, docs, config hashing, Docker create args, security-audit coverage, warnings, and focused tests while keeping raw Docker args unsupported.

options.title: Reject host IPC in core
options.body: Document GPU passthrough as the supported high-power Docker path and keep host IPC unavailable because it weakens sandbox isolation.

options.title: Define a broader namespace policy first
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define one policy for IPC, PID, network namespace joins, capabilities, and other dangerous Docker options.

recommendation.title: Approve a typed IPC break-glass field
recommendation.body: Add a narrow opt-in IPC setting with schema, docs, config hashing, Docker create args, security-audit coverage, warnings, and focused tests while keeping raw Docker args unsupported.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main policy-history signal for Docker namespace-sharing hardening is steipete's work on container namespace joins and dangerous Docker override handling.
